title: Fair Diversity Maximization with Few Representatives

problem.claim: Select k items that maximize minimum pairwise distance while ensuring each label is represented within a budget.

gap.claim: Existing fair diversity maximization methods do not provide the stated state-of-the-art approximation ratio for selecting only a constant number of items from each group.

contributions.claim: A randomized algorithm based on padded decompositions for fair diversity maximization with few representatives.
A multi-stage approach consisting of pruning, random cluster decomposition, and label assignment with representative selection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experimental verification of the algorithm's effectiveness on large datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diversity maximization seeks k diverse items, and its fair variant additionally requires adequate representation of each group.
The objective is to maximize minimum pairwise distance subject to label-representation budgets.
The focus is on cases requiring only a constant number of selected items from each group.
The proposed randomized algorithm uses padded decompositions and proceeds through pruning, decomposition, and assignment stages.
The authors report experiments on large datasets.

source_observation.claim: The algorithm separates same-label pruning, cluster decomposition, and representative assignment into distinct stages.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly structuring feasibility, diversity, and assignment constraints may simplify fair selection algorithms.

application.claim: Use staged preprocessing and constrained assignment when building selection systems that must balance diversity with group representation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this staged strategy generalizes beyond the stated metric, budgets, or few-representatives setting.

unknowns: The exact approximation guarantee definition and assumptions are unspecified.
The datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental results are unspecified.
The computational complexity and implementation details are unspecified.
